key_insight: For long-video QA, finding related events is not enough if the system cannot tell which exact object is being tracked over time. This paper argues for grounding “entity biographies” to preserve physical identity across hours or days.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the failure of timeline-based retrieval in long videos, where the same object can appear in disconnected events and different objects can share similar descriptions. This makes it hard to answer questions that depend on tracking a specific entity’s history.
method: Introduces Grounded Entity Biographies to represent an object’s identity-linked history across a long video.
Connects observations of the same physical entity across time instead of relying only on chronological event retrieval or text-derived entity mentions.
Evaluates how biography-aware retrieval improves long-video memory and question answering over timeline-only approaches.
impact: This helps AI systems answer object-centric questions in long videos more reliably, especially when identity continuity matters more than event order. For practitioners, it suggests a better memory design for surveillance, robotics, sports analysis, and multi-hour video understanding.
visual_elements: Timeline diagram showing events scattered across time with one object highlighted across multiple scenes
Side-by-side comparison of timeline retrieval vs grounded entity biography retrieval
Entity graph or identity chain linking the same object across different observations
Icons for object tracking, memory, and question answering
paper_title: Beyond the Timeline: Augmenting Long-Video Memory with Grounded Entity Biographies
paper_authors: Hui Ren, Lei Fan, Henry Pao, Han Guo, Zeeshan Zia
